definition: Vocational means related to training for a specific trade or occupation.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word vocational. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know vocational should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The prison's vocational workshop teaches carpentry and small-engine repair, and graduates leave with union cards as well as release papers.
A general education surveys a little of everything; vocational training aims every hour at one trade.
Applied courses point knowledge toward practice; vocational goes further, training you to walk straight onto one specific job.

Occupational describes what belongs to a job someone already holds — its hazards, its injuries, its therapy and licensing. Vocational looks the other way: training that prepares you for a trade you do not yet have. An occupational injury happens on the job; a vocational course comes before the job exists.

Hands-on describes how you learn: by doing the task rather than reading about it. Vocational describes what the learning is for: one specific trade or occupation. A chemistry lab is hands-on without being vocational, and a vocational bookkeeping course can be taught straight from a textbook.
